clue.text: Carry on to get record, just in time

parts.note: to carry on is to last, to keep going
a minute is a written record of a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going so as to get a recording made just before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the final moment before a deadline arrives is done barely in time.

clue.text: Strings or wind not loud initially

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for loud is taken away from the instruments

parts.note: flutes are wind instruments
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Asking for string instruments or woodwind, but quiet at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the F removed is the one at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked string instruments of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Tomb at sea if this is wrecked?

definitions.text: Tomb at sea if this is wrecked?

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the words smashed and reassembled in new order

explanation.surface: A ship that sinks becomes a watery grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a wrecked paddle vessel becomes a tomb at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered vessel which, if sunk, becomes a grave beneath the waves.

clue.text: A mythical metal disguised in a calculating way

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A legendary metal hidden in a scheming manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Done using calculation, by mathematics.

clue.text: Put out call — was first there

parts.note: call means need, as in no call for it
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: A phone call made, and someone was there before you.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means irritated or annoyed, as does put out.

clue.text: Near sign directing hospital visitors?

explanation.surface: A signpost close by points visitors through a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the word is the sign 'to wards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards means close to or near; and read as two words it is a hospital sign pointing to the wards.

clue.text: Offensive enterprise

explanation.surface: An attack mounted as a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A push is a military attack, a forward offensive, and also drive or initiative, the go-getting quality called enterprise.

clue.text: Sort of second class degree found in Oxford for example

explanation.surface: A degree classification earned at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: An upper second is a British degree grade; an Oxford is also a lace-up shoe, which has an upper.
explanation.definitionFit: A British degree's upper second class; and the top part of a shoe, which an Oxford shoe has.

clue.text: Man overcomes nuclear fallout, needing great effort

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit on top of the following piece

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: fallout suggests the letters falling out of order

explanation.surface: A man survives radioactive debris with enormous exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean tasks, like those of the Greek hero, demand enormous strength.

clue.text: For strain, effective method of prognosis

parts.note: a strain is a melody or tune
telling means effective, striking home

explanation.surface: A good technique for diagnosing a muscle strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Predicting what will happen to someone, as a clairvoyant does, is a way of forecasting.

clue.text: Centre of operations in war zone

explanation.surface: A headquarters set up in the middle of a combat area.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the hospital room where surgery is done; a theatre of war is the region where fighting takes place.

clue.text: Subject of one told by fisherman?

definitions.text: Subject of one told by fisherman?

parts.words: Subject of one told by fisherman?
parts.note: anglers famously exaggerate, telling a big lie about a big fish; the one word covers both the huge catch and the tall tale

explanation.surface: What an angler's story is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for something very large, such as a fish, and also for a blatant lie.

clue.text: A maiden embraced by posher clubman's servant

indicators.note: the outer word wraps around the pieces it embraces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: swell means smart or posh, so a sweller is a posher person
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is hugged by a snob's manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubman is Mr Pickwick of Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, founder of the Pickwick Club; his servant is the cockney Sam Weller.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Pickwick Papers this character is the loyal valet of Mr Pickwick, the club's founder.

clue.text: European port rejects Britain's routine procedure

indicators.note: rejecting is read as throwing back, so the whole run of letters is turned around

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, Britain
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: A port on the Continent turns away British red tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' reverses UK + RUT, giving TUR + KU.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a seaport on the southwest coast of Finland.

clue.text: Asian tree associated with a city in India

parts.note: the poon is an East Indian tree whose timber is used for masts

explanation.surface: A tree from Asia linked with an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Poona, now usually spelt Pune, is a city in Maharashtra.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona is the older name of Pune, a large city in western India.

clue.text: Trim sort of suit for musical director

parts.note: piping is a decorative trim, and to pipe is to trim with it
in bridge, spades and hearts are the major suits

explanation.surface: A neat outfit for a conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a pipe band directs the bagpipers.

clue.text: Stop fighting — expecting ring come-back?

explanation.surface: Breaking off combat while waiting for a counter-punch in the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: breaking off an engagement means the ring is expected back.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from combat; also to end a betrothal, after which the engagement ring is returned.

clue.text: Indian relics, for example, a rani came out for

indicators.note: out means the letters come out of their order

explanation.surface: A princess turned up for some Indian artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are objects and artefacts associated with American history and culture.

clue.text: Aristocrat gives girl extra name

parts.note: Patricia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nobleman gives a young woman an additional name.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of Rome's noble class, hence any person of high birth.

clue.text: Had to have such a change? It's acute

definitions.text: Had to have such a change?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a big shift was forced, and finding it sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Had is have in the past tense, so moving from have to had is a change in tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, a change of verb form; whole, intense means acute or extreme.

clue.text: Poet's fresh start

parts.note: new means fresh
to bolt is to start or jump suddenly

explanation.surface: A writer's new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Newbolt wrote 'Drake's Drum' and 'Vitai Lampada'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Newbolt was an English writer of patriotic verse.

clue.text: Wooden old actor needs new finale

indicators.note: a finale comes at the end, so this piece is added last of all

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A stiff veteran performer needs a fresh ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a criticism of the actor but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is the term for small domestic objects made of wood, and as an adjective means made of timber.

clue.text: Vehicles — some immediately pulled out

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A few cars were withdrawn straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' tells you the letters are extracted from 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Media are means or channels of communication, vehicles in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Apprentice cook

explanation.surface: A trainee chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's devil was an errand boy or junior helper; to devil food is to cook it with hot spices.

clue.text: Fabric attached to house (apart from front)

parts.note: to can mean attached, as a door pushed to

indicators.note: everything but the first letter of the word for house is used

parts.note: a dwelling is a house

explanation.surface: Cloth fixed to a home, though not its facade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from front' removes D, leaving WELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry cloth, the absorbent looped cotton used for bath sheets, is a kind of material.

clue.text: Leading member of party secured by rope, sey

definitions.text: member of party secured by rope, sey

explanation.surface: The head of a mountaineering party, tied on with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide is to lead; and a mountain guide is one of a climbing team roped together.

clue.text: Live broadcast within a month, for athletic event

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the month

parts.note: Jan is short for January

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A sports event shown live during one month of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges LIVE to VELI, which goes inside JAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the spear is a field event in track-and-field athletics.

clue.text: Result of business folding out East

definitions.text: Result of business folding out East

parts.words: Result of business folding out East
parts.note: reads as a firm going bust in Asia, but means paper folded into shapes, the Japanese craft

explanation.surface: The consequence of a company collapsing in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of paper folding produces models such as cranes.

clue.text: Deliver a judgment, in principle

explanation.surface: A judge pronouncing a decision on a point of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to give a judicial decision; a rule is a governing principle or regulation.

clue.text: One mark added to money scale

indicators.note: these pieces are tacked on after the money

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a unit of money
I is the Roman numeral for one
a grade is a mark given for work

explanation.surface: A single score combined with cash to make a measuring system.
explanation.definitionFit: Celsius temperature scale, divided into a hundred degrees between freezing and boiling.
